messages.subject: Mentors needed for Automatic Differentiation project
messages.subject_clean: Mentors needed for Automatic Differentiation project
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am proposing a project for 2018 GSoC-R: Automatic Differentiation in R through Julia.

Automatic differentiation has important applications in many fields like optimization, machine learning, Bayesian statistics, differential equations and etc.
Julia <https://julialang.org/> is a high-performance language for numerical computing.
While there is a lack of automatic differentiation package in R, Julia  has quite mature automatic differentiation packages, like ForwardDiff.jl <https://github.com/JuliaDiff/ForwardDiff.jl> for forward mode AD and ReverseDiff.jl <https://github.com/JuliaDiff/ReverseDiff.jl> for reverse mode AD. The aim of this project is to develop an R wrapper for the Julia AD packages.

The idea page is here:

https://github.com/Non-Contradiction/AD-R-GSOC

I'm looking for interested mentors.

Thank you very much.

Best,
Changcheng Li

messages.subject: Re: Mentors needed for Automatic Differentiation project
messages.subject_clean: Mentors needed for Automatic Differentiation project
messages.body_plain:
I may be willing, but may not be available all the time, so would need a co-mentor.

There's some symbolic and sort-of automatic differentiation in package nlsr. I also mentored
a student some years back, but his level of expertise was, I think, too limited and he
followed some unprofitable lines of coding. Also we had very poor communications, as he
was in India but not in one place for more than a couple of weeks.

Since there are already Julia AD packages, this project may have a better chance.

A useful interface to AD would be using the mechanism already in place for the package
optimx THAT IS ON R-FORGE. The CRAN package doesn't yet have all the features. In the
function optimr(), by specifying gr="something in quotes" the method for the gradient
is currently one of several gradient approximations. so "grfwd" does a forward difference
etc. "grnd" uses numDeriv. Something like "grauto" could do automatic differentiation.
The optimr() function would be a vehicle to interface to other solvers (that was it's
design intention), thereby saving multiple interfacing tasks.

Changcheng: Let me know.

Anyone interesting in co-mentor: Let both of us know!

Best, John Nash

messages.body_plain:
Dear John Nash,

Thank you for the information. I checked about nlsr and may make some comparison of AD with nlsr in the project.

I tried optimr and optimx on R-FORGE. I had some problems with optimx, but optimr is working well.
It seems to me that just writing some function in package optextras like `grauto` for AD,
`grautofwd` for forward mode AD and etc. can make AD work in optimr() and it is really wonderful.

I'm the maintainer of JuliaCall, which embedds Julia in R, and AD through Julia seems promising.
I'll try my best for the project.

Thank you very much.

Best,
Changcheng

messages.subject: Co-Mentors needed for R User Groups & R-Ladies Groups worldwide project
messages.subject_clean: Co-Mentors needed for R User Groups & R-Ladies Groups worldwide project
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am proposing a project focused on a data driven application for R User Groups and R-Ladies Groups worldwide.

The idea is based on the suggestion by David Smith here: http://blog.revolutionanalytics.com/2017/01/list-of-r-conferences-and-user-groups.html
and based on the list maintained by Colin Gillespie here: https://jumpingrivers.github.io/meetingsR/r-user-groups.html

In general, the work involves data curation, storage, and interactivity using Shiny/Dashboards.
Visualization using maps, etc is also proposed and any other data-related tasks mentors would come up with.
We hope that this project would produce an easily reusable data-set on the user groups that the R Community could use for
several other analyses.

Colin Gillespie is a mentor for this project.

So, we need more co-mentors.

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: R GSoC 2018
messages.body_plain:
We have about 48 hours left before student applications close for this
year.

Students:

You need to finalize your applications on the summerofcode website.

We cannot consider an application that is not in 'final' state, and
Google program rules do not allow you to update the application after
you have finalized it.

Don't leave this to the last minute, if you miss the deadline, we can't
help you.

If you receive comments from mentors on your draft applications, please
address them in the comments on the Google Doc draft and in the text
that becomes your final proposal.  Program rules require us to
primarily consider the actual text of your final project proposal.

Mentors:

You should all have received emails from Google inviting you to join
GSoC as a mentor for R.  If you do not have such an email, please
contact Toby and me.

Once applications close, we need you to:

1. comment on all applications for your projects as soon as possible

These comments are only visible to other R GSoC mentors.

2. comment on as many of the student applications for other projects as
you feel you have some interest, insight, or skill in.

Your comments will help Toby and me evaluate the overall impact,
interest, and likelihood of success of the student projects.

3. select 'Want to Mentor' for your top choice (only) for any projects
for which you are listed as a mentor.  Toby and I will not consider
projects for slots until all the mentors have commented on the proposal
and selected 'Want to Mentor'.

As always, if you have any questions, please reach out to Toby and me
and we will do what we can to assist.

Thanks,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

Vissarion, (and a note for all the students later)

First, while there is no student identifying information here, so we're
fine. I do want to remind everyone to *never* discuss the particulars of
a student proposal here.  We should be commenting on the proposals on
the Google summerofcode.withgoogle.com <http://summerofcode.withgoogle.com> site. Private questions about
proposals should go to Toby (CC'd) and me.

On the question for Mentors:

Yes, you will select 'want to mentor' on your top choice.

No, we can't make substitutions later, unless a student is chosen by two
orgs for competing projects.

Students:

This means that if you withdraw after selection, you are depriving the R
organization of a slot that we could have awarded to another student.
Please be mature and professional.  If you are going to take a different
internship in preference to participating with GSoC in R, please
withdraw before final selection. GSoC is a very prestigious and
competitive program, and I think it looks better on a resume than most
other internships (and you can show later employers what you did!).  But
please do everyone the courtesy of withdrawing before selection if you
are going to preference a different internship over GSoC so that another
student has a chance.

messages.subject: R GSoC next steps
messages.body_plain:
Applications have now closed, and the next two weeks are about proposal
review.

Students:

Mostly, expect silence during this period, sorry.  If you do get
inquiries from mentors, please answer.  If you get inquiries from
Google, absolutely respond as soon as possible.

Mentors:

This is the time we need input from all our mentors.

If don't have your invitation to the summerofcode site, please let me
and Toby know as soon as possible, and we'll correct it.

We need all mentors to review as many proposals as you feel qualified
to comment on.  Please leave comments on the proposal in the comment
section at the bottom of the proposal page on the summerofcode website.

If the proposal is for your project idea, we need you to give us even
more information on what you think of the proposal, and why you think a
project slot for this proposal should be high on our list to ask Google
to fund.

If the proposal is for your project idea, we need you and your co-
mentor(s) to select 'Want to Mentor' in the upper right.

If you received more than one application for your project idea, please
 only select 'Want to Mentor' for your top choice.  Please make sure to
describe relative ranking (and why you feel that way) in the comments
section for each of your received proposals.

Toby and I will not consider a project for slotting if all mentors
haven't chimed in on their feelings on the project, and selected 'want
to mentor'.

Remember that per Google program rules we cannot discuss with students
anything about their probability of getting a slot, or how competitive
they are with other students.  At this point, we must evaluate the
Final PDF as submitted by the student.

As always, please don't hesitate to email me or Toby with any
questions.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock
